claims.text: In donhang, the API server, etcd and kube-scheduler run only on donhang-control-plane; while it is paused, kubectl get nodes --request-timeout=10s fails.

While the control plane is unreachable, the kubelets keep running the containers already on their nodes and a NodePort Service keeps forwarding to the Pods behind it, so echo-ip still answers on its node port, called from donhang-lb-client, a container on kind's Docker network.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Components (kubelet, kube-proxy); capture control-plane-ha.txt line 5 'echo-ip-... saw'; don-hang stage-3 scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh lines 38-42

claims.text: Every read and change of a cluster object goes through the API server, which stores the objects in etcd; with no API server reachable, nothing in the cluster can be read or changed with kubectl.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Components (kube-apiserver, etcd); Concepts > Overview > The Kubernetes API

claims.text: A kind cluster config with several nodes of role: control-plane creates a control plane on each of them, each with its own API server and its own etcd member (stacked etcd), plus scheduler and controller manager.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Configuration > Nodes (multiple control-plane nodes / HA); don-hang stage-3 deploy/k8s/kind-ha-config.yaml comment lines 2-4

claims.text: With more than one control-plane node, kind starts an extra load balancer container (named <cluster>-external-load-balancer) in front of the API servers and writes its address, a port on 127.0.0.1 of the host, into the kubeconfig.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Configuration > Nodes (HA control plane, external load balancer); capture control-plane-ha.txt lines 14-19

claims.text: A highly available control plane on your own machines needs one address in front of its API servers that you provide, such as a load balancer.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Setup > Production environment > Creating Highly Available Clusters with kubeadm > Create load balancer for kube-apiserver

claims.text: Every etcd member holds a copy of the same data, and etcd commits a change only once a majority (quorum) of its members has it.
claims.source_hint: etcd.io/docs/v3.6: FAQ > What is failure tolerance? / Why an odd number of cluster members?; Learning > Data model

claims.text: Quorum of an n-member etcd cluster is floor(n/2)+1: three members need two and tolerate one failure; four need three and tolerate one; five need three and tolerate two.
claims.source_hint: etcd.io/docs/v3.6: FAQ > What is failure tolerance? (table of cluster size, majority, failure tolerance)

claims.text: With one of donhang-ha's three control-plane nodes paused, kubectl get nodes still works through the load balancer and still lists the paused node, whose Node object stays in etcd.

With one node paused, control-plane-ha.sh retries get nodes up to ten times, three seconds apart, because the first requests after a pause can fail; its comment, not the lesson, names the load balancer's health checks as the cause.
claims.source_hint: don-hang stage-3 scripts/k8s/control-plane-ha.sh lines 59-68 (retry loop and comment)

claims.text: With two of three members stopped, the remaining etcd member has no quorum: it can neither commit a change nor confirm the latest data that the API server's requests need. That API server keeps running, but kubectl requests time out or fail with an error.
claims.source_hint: etcd.io/docs/v3.6: FAQ / Op guide > Failure modes (majority failure: cluster cannot accept writes); capture control-plane-ha.txt lines 28-31

claims.text: When a control plane's etcd runs on its control-plane nodes, run an odd number of them: an even number adds a machine that can fail without raising the number of failures survived.
kubectl --kubeconfig <file> uses that kubeconfig instead of the default; --request-timeout=15s makes a request give up after 15 seconds.

crictl ps, run inside a kind node, lists the containers the kubelet started there; with --name kube-apiserver --state running -q it prints the IDs of running containers named kube-apiserver, one per line.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Debug cluster > Debugging Kubernetes nodes with crictl; crictl ps --help

claims.text: Each kind node is a Docker container; docker pause freezes every process in it, so the API server and etcd member on a paused node stop responding until docker unpause.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Design / Quick Start (nodes are containers); Docker CLI reference: docker container pause

claims.text: kind-ha-config.yaml lists three role: control-plane nodes and no worker, each with the same kindest/node:v1.34.11 image pinned by digest as donhang's kind-config.yaml.
control-plane-ha.sh keeps donhang-ha's kubeconfig in secrets/, unpauses every paused node and deletes donhang-ha on exit, even when it stops early (trap cleanup EXIT).
kind's API server listens on a random open host port by default, so the port in the kubeconfig changes between runs.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Configuration > Networking > API Server
